chapter: Father and the brass band tradition
title: Outstanding early parade drummers: Henry Martin, Red Dugal, Black Benny
summary: He names the snare and bass drummers he followed as a boy and says they also played orchestra drums in district clubs.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Did you ever play bass drum in parades?
No, I never did.
Just snare drum.
Snare drum.
When you were young, who were some of the outstanding snare drummers and bass drum players, even before you started playing?
Oh, well, I can tell you, that was Henry Martin. I know you have heard of him. I've heard of him.
I've never got one.
Red Dugal.
You ever heard of him? Never, I've heard of him, but never knew much about him. You know anything about him, especially? No, he's a fine drummer. What part of town he came from?
He came from around the Red Light District. Bienvenida, Vilcona, Liberty. Benny.
Yeah.
I know his first name. I know you know Benny. Like Benny. Like Benny.
Who were these guys playing with, like Henry Martin, Red Dugal, and Black Benny?

Well, they was playing with the Armored Band, Brass Band. All three of them? Yeah, but not three drummers at one time. Different bands, different brass bands they played with. Excelsior Band, Olympia Band, Imperial Band.
Did they all play one particular drum, like snare or bass, or did they play them both?
No, they played one drum in the parade. That's all snare drum.
Well, for instance, which drum would Henry Martin play?
Snare drum. What about Benny? Benny would play bass drum.
I heard you played bass drum.
Well, yeah, that's a fact of them, but I know of them. I followed them around.
What about Red Dugal? What did he play?
Snare drum. Well, he played orchestra drums too, you know, in orchestra. Henry Martin played orchestra drums too.
What orchestras would they play with?
Well, they was playing in nightclubs in the district, see. But I was young again, I just can't remember.
